title: Axiom: Runbook Mesh + Idempotent Steplets for Safe Admin Automation
creator: Asha Patel
description:
Problem: Support engineers rely on ad-hoc scripts and long runbooks composed in docs. This leads to inconsistent remediation, hard-to-replay actions, and production risk.

Goal: Build 'Axiom' — a runbook mesh that composes small, idempotent 'steplets' into deterministic, auditable task graphs. The system should power one-click remediations, safe dry-runs, and fine-grained telemetry for post-incident analysis.

Non-goals: Not replacing long-term orchestration platforms (Argo/Circle) for batch workflows; not a general-purpose job scheduler. Focus is on human-in-the-loop admin utilities and support automation for SRE/Support flows.
acceptance_criteria: Steplet registry exists with typed inputs and idempotency metadata documented
Runbook mesh can compose >=5 steplets into a single task graph and execute with ordered retries
Dry-run mode executes validations and side-effect checks without mutating production resources
All executions produce provenance records (who ran, inputs, resolved outputs, KV cache diff) viewable in Console
Safety gates: RBAC + approval hooks block destructive steplets by default
Automated rollback on failed critical step with clear postmortem payload created
technical_design: Steplet model: lightweight executable unit with schema (inputs -> outputs), idempotency token, side-effect annotations, soft/hard rollback handlers
Registry: Postgres-backed index with per-step versioning and signed manifests; REST lookup endpoint and SDK helper
Executor: Stateful worker that compiles steplet graph into safe transactional window (prefers idempotent operations, uses compare-and-swap where available)
Safety layer: RBAC + canary policy (run N steps in dry-run, then gated approval); destructive steplets flagged and require 2FA approval in Console
Observability: emit structured events to telemetry pipeline (trace id, steplet id, latency, tokens consumed, KV-cache hits), surface on per-execution dashboard
Migration: wrapper for existing admin scripts - adaptors to convert legacy scripts into steplets with minimal shim
Fallbacks: configurable fallback steplets (eg. call safer lower-privilege path) for service degradation scenarios
tasks: Design steplet manifest schema and idempotency semantics (Asha/Luca) — DONE
Implement registry API and CLI publisher (backend) — IN PROGRESS
Build executor prototype with dry-run and replay support (worker team) — IN PROGRESS
Console: execution view + approval modal + provenance card (frontend) — TODO
Security review and threat model (Security team) — PENDING
Convert 3 canonical runbooks (node alloc, model-evict, routing-fallback) into steplets for pilot — TODO
E2E test harness + chaos scenarios (SRE) — TODO
risks_and_tradeoffs: Tradeoff: strict idempotency rules reduce expressiveness of quick scripts — mitigated by providing helper primitives for common safe ops
Operational risk: central registry becomes a critical dependency; mitigated via replication + local fallback cache
Performance: orchestration adds millisecond overhead per step; measured impact should be acceptable for human-initiated flows but flagged for high-throughput automation
Security: steplets may expose privileged operations; we require signed manifests and review for high-impact versions
rollback_plan: Executor writes a reversible checkpoint before destructive steps; rollback steplet is invoked automatically on failure
If automated rollback fails, raise a high-priority incident and provide a safety-mode playbook in Console with step-by-step manual remediation
Snapshot metadata stored in audit log for forensic analysis
telemetry_and_ksis: Mean latency per steplet and per graph
Number of approval rejections and average approval time
KV-cache hit rate for reused outputs
